subject: science
domain: Motion and Stability: Forces and Interactions

items.prompt:
Electric and magnetic forces can act:
A) Only when objects touch
B) Between objects that are not touching
C) Only in water
D) Only on living things
items.answer: B) Between objects that are not touching

steps: They are non-contact forces that act across a distance.

items.prompt:
As two magnets move closer together, the force between them:
A) Gets weaker
B) Gets stronger
C) Disappears
D) Stays exactly the same

steps: Smaller distance means a stronger magnetic force.

items.prompt:
Which factor affects the strength of a magnetic force?
A) The color of the magnet
B) The distance between the magnets
C) The day of the week
D) The magnet's name
items.answer: B) The distance between the magnets

steps: Distance affects the magnetic force strength.

items.prompt:
To test how distance affects magnetic force fairly, a student should change:
A) Many things at once
B) Only the distance
C) Only the color
D) Nothing

steps: Changing one variable isolates its effect.

items.prompt:
Which change would increase the electric force between two charged objects?
A) Moving them farther apart
B) Increasing the charge
C) Removing all charge
D) Painting them

steps: More charge increases the electric force.

items.prompt:
A stronger magnet lifts more paper clips than a weak one at the same distance. This shows that:
A) Distance is the only factor
B) Magnet strength affects the force
C) Color matters
D) Nothing affects the force
items.answer: B) Magnet strength affects the force

steps: Comparing at equal distance isolates magnet strength.

items.prompt:
Why are electric and magnetic forces classified as non-contact forces?
A) They require direct touching
B) They act between objects across a distance without contact
C) They only work on metals that touch
D) They are not real forces
items.answer: B) They act between objects across a distance without contact

steps: Non-contact forces act across a distance without the objects touching.

items.prompt:
A student finds a magnet's pull weakens with distance and strengthens with a stronger magnet. The best conclusion is:
A) Only one factor affects magnetic force
B) Both distance and magnet strength affect the force
C) Neither factor matters
D) Magnets never attract
items.answer: B) Both distance and magnet strength affect the force

steps: Both distance and strength affect the magnetic force.
